text: dsh-oliver-qol 是面向 DSH Web 客户端的体验增强插件，在会话行菜单和设置页中加入功能。用户可从会话菜单发起永久删除，服务端按会话及其子会话处理存储，并清理相关缓存和部分引用状态；Extend settings 页面提供 OpenCode Go 网页搜索开关、模型选择和独立代理地址设置。搜索关闭时使用 DSH 内置搜索 provider，开启后将查询交给 OpenCode Go。适合需要清理会话或希望配置网页搜索模型与代理的 DSH Web 用户。启用搜索需要可解析的 OpenCode Go API key，并会连接 opencode.ai。

dsh-oliver-qol adds session deletion and OpenCode Go search to DSH Web. Delete sessions and subagent descendants from the session menu. Extend settings controls search, model, and proxy. Disabled search uses DSH’s built-in provider; enabled search sends queries to opencode.ai and requires API key.
想从会话列表里永久删除一个不再需要的 DSH 会话。
能不能删除会话时把它派生的子 agent 会话也一起清理？
I want to route DSH web searches through OpenCode Go and choose a search model and proxy.
dsh-oliver-qol 的功能「删除会话」：在会话行菜单选择删除并进入确认流程，客户端向主机发送会话标识；主机删除该会话及子会话存储，并清理关联缓存和引用记录。
dsh-oliver-qol 的功能「OpenCode Go 网页搜索」：在设置页启用后可选模型和专用代理；web_search 查询交给 OpenCode Go，关闭时使用 DSH 内置搜索。
dsh-oliver-qol 使用 OpenCode Go 搜索时，会把查询文本发送至 opencode.ai；搜索启用后需提供能解析的 API key 引用，默认环境变量名为 OPENCODE_API_KEY。

dsh-oliver-qol README · dsh-oliver-qol：Personal quality-of-life features for the [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (dsh), bundled as one plugin. Each feature lives in its own module under `src/features/`, carries its own config section, locale namespace, route prefix, and tests, and never imports another feature.

dsh-oliver-qol README · dsh-oliver-qol：| Feature | State | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `session-delete` | implemented | Permanently deletes a stored session (log, projection cache, workspace accounting, orphaned `.agent-teams` state, task-board execution references) from the session row menu, cascading into its subagent child sessions |
| `extend-settings` | implemented | Adds an **Extend settings** tab (last) to the settings page; it declares the `settings.extend-settings.item` list slot every QoL setting row registers into |
| `opencode-search` | implemented | The row in that tab: routes the built-in `web_search` tool through OpenCode Go — endpoint and key reference follow the `dsh-opencode-go` plugin settings, while the search model and the proxy address (host + port) are set in the row itself and touch nothing else. Off by default; while off it delegates to the built-in DeepSeek search provider |

dsh-oliver-qol README · Compatibility：Built against dsh `0.2.0-rc.2`. dsh APIs are pre-stable, so the manifest declares open-ended floors (`>=0.2.0-rc.2`) instead of pins: a dsh upgrade must not silently drop the bundle, and a real API break surfaces as an error to fix rather than as a plugin that vanished.

dsh-oliver-qol README · Install：The plugin is a dsh bundle: its `package.json` declares `dsh.bundle` (host half) and `dsh.client` (browser half).

```bat
:: from npm (the supported path — the published tarball already contains lib/)
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-oliver-qol

:: from a local checkout (development loop)

dsh-oliver-qol README · Install：Install it as an **npm package**, never as a `github:` dependency. A git install fetches source, so pnpm rebuilds it on every install, needs a working `pnpm` on `PATH`, needs an `allowBuilds` entry keyed by the exact commit URL, and leaves the lockfile pinned to the old commit — enough to make the plugin manager report a failure even though the install succeeded. The published package ships `lib/`, so none of that applies. See [docs/DISTRIBUTION.md](docs/DISTRIBUTION.md) for the full evidence.

dsh-oliver-qol README · Install：Restart dsh after adding, updating, or removing the plugin. The bundle patch (`cordis.patch.yml`) mounts one row (`id: oliver-qol`, `name: dsh-oliver-qol`) and points the web seam's `searchProvider` at the `opencode-go` provider this bundle registers.

dsh-oliver-qol README · Release：```bat
npm version minor   :: patch | minor | major
npm publish         :: prepublishOnly rebuilds lib/ and runs the tests
```

`lib/` is gitignored and built at publish time; it is **not** committed.

dsh-oliver-qol README · Configuration：```yaml
- id: oliver-qol
  config:
    sessionDelete:
      sessionsRoot: <path>          # default: dshHomePath('sessions')

`sessionDelete.sessionsRoot` must match the `root` of the profile's `session-persistence-jsonl` row (`$DSH_HOME/sessions` by default). If a deployment moves that root, set both.

dsh-oliver-qol README · Configuration：`removeOrphanedTeamState` and `pruneTaskBoardReferences` clean the two pieces of state that only *reference* a session, after its log is gone. Both are best-effort: a failure is warned and skipped, never surfaced as a failed delete, because the session the user asked to delete is already deleted.

dsh-oliver-qol README · Configuration：- **AgentTeams** keeps `<workspace>/.agent-teams/<teamId>/` (`team.json` + member inboxes) under the directory the session ran in. When the delete removes a team's `captainSessionId`, that team can never be resumed — the plugin treats the captain as its only owner key — so the directory is removed. A team that lost only a *member* while its captain lives may still be running or resumable, so it is **reported, not edited**: rewriting `team.json` from here would race the plugin for a team it still owns.
- **Task board** keeps `$DSH_HOME/task-board/ledger-v2.json`, and every card's `executions[]` entry pins the session that performed it. Only those dangling records are dropped. Cards, columns, prompts, schedules and open executions (`endedAt` absent) are never touched, and an unknown `schemaVersion` is refused rather than pattern-matched. The replace is optimistic — the file is re-read immediately before the write, and any concurrent change aborts the pass — so losing one cleanup pass is possible and harmless; clobbering the board's newest state is not.

dsh-oliver-qol README · Configuration：`opencodeSearch` is a live section: the **Extend settings** row writes it without a restart. Per search, the provider reads the `baseURL` and `apiKeyEnv` that the `opencode-go` profile row (the `dsh-opencode-go` plugin) currently resolves, and resolves that credential reference through the credentials service — the same `OPENCODE_API_KEY` the chat route uses. Those are the only two facts it borrows: the proxy is the row's own (`proxyUrl`/`proxyPort`), so nothing configured for chat traffic reaches a search, and nothing a search sets reaches chat. Without that plugin the documented defaults apply (`https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1`, `OPENCODE_API_KEY`).

dsh-oliver-qol README · Configuration：`proxyUrl` takes a host (`127.0.0.1`), a host and port (`127.0.0.1:7890`), or a full URL with a scheme (`socks5://127.0.0.1`); a bare host is read as HTTP. `proxyPort` is a decimal 1–65535 and overrides any port inside `proxyUrl`; empty means the search uses whatever port the address carries. Both empty connects directly. The Extend-settings row commits each half on blur or Enter — one typed address is one write — and refuses a port the host would refuse, so the row and the next search cannot disagree.

dsh-oliver-qol README · How the search selection works：The bundle patch points the web seam at this provider (`web.searchProvider: opencode-go`). While the Extend-settings row is off, the provider delegates every search to the built-in `deepseek-official` provider, so installing this plugin changes nothing until the feature is enabled. A deployment can drop the `web` override from `cordis.patch.yml` (or its own profile patch) to ignore the provider entirely.

dsh-oliver-qol README · How the search selection works：One search is one auxiliary model turn against the OpenCode Go endpoint with the native `web_search_20250305` server tool — latency plus tokens count against the Go usage quota. `deepseek-v4.1-flash` is verified end-to-end through this provider (10 structured results, ~10k input tokens); other Go model ids are selectable but unverified for server-side search. OpenCode Go requires `x-opencode-session` on every request: the provider sends the initiating conversation's id and, outside a conversation, one stable per-instance id.

dsh-oliver-qol README · Development：```sh
pnpm install
pnpm test          # vitest
pnpm typecheck     # tsc, no emit
pnpm lint          # oxlint

`lib/` is not committed. The client bundle is one CJS artifact wrapped in `window.__ModuleLoader__.load({ id: 'dsh-oliver-qol', factory })`; platform modules (`react`, `react/jsx-runtime`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-primitives`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-store`) stay external and resolve through the injected `require`.

dsh-oliver-qol README · Development：Adding a feature: create `src/features/<name>/` (with its own `client/` half when it has UI), then add one line to `src/features/index.ts` and one to `src/client/index.ts`. A client-only feature skips `src/features/index.ts` and adds only its client line. A setting row registers one entry into the `settings.extend-settings.item` slot declared by `extend-settings` — the slot key (and nothing else) is the contract between the hub and the row. Keep features independent — share code only through a `src/shared/` module that at least two features actually use.

dsh-oliver-qol README · Manual acceptance (needs a dsh restart)：1. Open a session's "..." menu — `Delete session` sits below `Archive session`, in red.
2. Delete a plain session: confirm, then check the row disappears and `$DSH_HOME/sessions/<project>/<id>/` is gone.
3. Delete a session that spawned subagents: the dialog names the child count; confirm the child directories and their `session_projcache` rows are gone.
4. Delete the session that is currently open: it is stopped and released first; expect the conversation view to clear.
5. Delete an archived session from the archived filter.
6. Check `$DSH_HOME/storages/session_projcache` no longer holds rows for the deleted ids, and that workspace accounting (`$DSH_HOME/storages/workspace.json`) dropped them.
6a. Delete the captain of a team that ran in a workspace: `<workspace>/.agent-teams/<teamId>/` is gone. Delete only one member and keep the captain: the directory stays and the log carries one `team <teamId>: member session(s) deleted but the captain lives` warning.
6b. Delete a session that the task board ran: its card in `$DSH_HOME/task-board/ledger-v2.json` keeps its title, column, prompt and schedule, while the `executions[]

dsh-oliver-qol README · Known limitations：- Deletion is permanent; there is no undo. Use archive for reversible hiding.
- A session written by another dsh process at the same time fails loudly (`session-delete/busy`) on Windows file locks; retry after that process stops.
- Deleting the currently open session relies on the shipped archive-driven release of the main view; if the client does not release it in time, the request answers `busy` and can be retried.
- The JSONL storage layout (project directory + encoded session segment) is the only format coupling; it lives in `src/features/session-delete/jsonl-layout.ts` and `removal.ts` and must be re-checked on dsh upgrades.
- The two reference cleanups couple to *other plugins'* on-disk layouts, both isolated in their own module and both re-checkable on their plugin's upgrades: `.agent-teams/<teamId>/team.json` (`team-state.ts`) and `task-board/ledger-v2.json` schema 6 (`task-board.ts`). Neither plugin is a dependency — a missing directory, an unknown schema, or an unparsable file leaves the delete behaving exactly as before.
